what: `AttributeValue` — pi-telemetry's scalar/array union vs @opentelemetry/api's `AttributeValue`
resolution: KEEP pi's name and shape verbatim — it is part of the copied public API and renaming it breaks every downstream pi schema. No compile conflict today because omp never re-exports OTEL's `AttributeValue` from a barrel (only `Attributes`, `Span`, `SpanKind`, `SpanStatusCode`, `Tracer`, `trace` are re-exported, telemetry.ts:2106). Constraint handed to the agent spec: when omp's agent adopts TelemetryContext, alias OTEL's at the import site (`import { type AttributeValue as OtelAttributeValue }`) and do NOT `export * from "@oh-my-pi/pi-telemetry"` inside packages/agent/src/index.ts, because that barrel already does `export * from "./telemetry"` (index.ts:24) and a future `AttributeValue` there would be an ambiguous star export.

what: `SpanOptions` and `SpanStatus` — pi's `{name, attributes?}` / `{status:'ok'|'error'}` vs OTEL's `{attributes?,links?,startTime?,kind?}` / `{code,message?}`
omp_anchor: packages/agent/test/run-summary.test.ts:27-28 (imported from @opentelemetry/api), :37, :45, :83 — this test hand-rolls a fake `Tracer` with `startSpan(name, options?: SpanOptions)` and `setStatus(status: SpanStatus)`
resolution: KEEP pi's names verbatim. The two live in different modules today so nothing collides. Do NOT 'unify' them — pi's are the callback-scoped contract, OTEL's are the immediate-span wire type, and merging them would force one of the two test doubles to change. Same barrel constraint as above: the agent spec must use explicit aliased named re-exports (exactly what pi does at packages/agent/src/index.ts:19-37) rather than a star re-export of the telemetry package.

what: `startSpan` — pi's callback-scoped `startSpan(options, callback) => Promise<T>` (span lives only for the callback) vs omp's immediate `startSpan(telemetry, kind, name, options)` helper and OTEL's `Tracer.startSpan(name, options, ctx)`
omp_anchor: packages/agent/src/telemetry.ts:466 (module-private helper) and :500 (`telemetry.tracer.startSpan(...)`); 14 `startSpan` refs total across omp
resolution: KEEP pi's shape. Same name, opposite lifetime model — this is the highest-risk mental collision in the whole migration because both are called `startSpan` and both produce something called a span. Mitigation for the copy step: this package defines no bare local `startSpan` binding, so nothing inside packages/telemetry conflicts. The real hazard is a FUTURE file that imports both `TelemetryContext` and omp's agent telemetry; that file must not alias either import to the bare name `startSpan`.

what: `TelemetrySpan` (pi) vs `TelemetrySpanKind` (omp) — near-identical names, unrelated symbols
resolution: No action, and no rename. `TelemetrySpanKind` is a 4-value string union about OTEL operation names; `TelemetrySpan` is the recording interface. Renaming either would diverge from pi for no benefit. Listed here only so a future grep for 'TelemetrySpan' does not report a false collision.

what: CONCEPTUAL, not textual: omp has TWO existing telemetry things and pi adds a third. They are not duplicates and must not be merged.
pi_anchor: packages/telemetry/src/index.ts:14-22 (the callback contract) + README.md:365-372 ('Pi Package Integration')
omp_anchor: packages/agent/src/telemetry.ts (2114 lines, an OTEL EMITTER that actually produces @opentelemetry/api Span objects and exports to OTLP) and packages/stats (a LOCAL SQLite dashboard, 74 KB db.ts, 19 KB parser.ts, 41 KB trace.ts — reads session JSONL, never sends anything)
resolution: KEEP ALL THREE, in a strict dependency order: (1) `@oh-my-pi/pi-telemetry` = the vendor-neutral CONTRACT — zero I/O, zero vendor, zero network, just 'what a span is'. (2) `packages/agent/src/telemetry.ts` = the omp EMITTER that binds that contract to OTEL/OTLP. (3) `packages/stats` = the LOCAL READER that turns session logs into a dashboard. Stats is local (nothing leaves the machine); agent telemetry is remote (OTLP); pi telemetry is neither — it is the vocabulary the other two will eventually share. The integration point is `RecordedTelemetrySpan` (memory.ts:16): it is the normalized shape any omp emitter must produce to be covered by `createTelemetryAdapterConformance`, which is how OTEL and in-memory become provably equivalent. Do NOT port pi's emitter into omp's OTEL file and do NOT make stats depend on telemetry yet — wiring the contract into omp's agent is the AGENT spec's job, not telemetry's.

what: readStoredCredential — SAME NAME, DIFFERENT SIGNATURE. pi: readStoredCredential(provider, authPath) at packages/coding-agent/src/core/auth-storage.ts:496. omp: readStoredCredential(provider) at packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/legacy-pi-coding-agent-shim.ts:1469, which resolves auth.json through AuthStorage.create() and takes no path.
resolution: KEEP omp's. The whole point of the eval harness is to read a credential from an ISOLATED agent dir before the session exists; omp's version reads the process-global AuthStorage and would silently use the developer's real ~/.omp/agent/auth.json — leaking the developer's credentials into a container that then drops privileges. omp's signature is also the one the 2-arg call would compile against only by accident. Resolve the path explicitly (authPath = join(hostAgentDir,'auth.json')) and read the file directly, or add an optional second parameter to omp's function.

what: CreateAgentSessionOptions.tools / .noTools DO NOT EXIST in omp. pi's harness types PiCodingAgentHarnessOptions.tools and .noTools as CreateAgentSessionOptions['tools'] / ['noTools'] and forwards them to createAgentSessionFromServices. omp's CreateAgentSessionOptions (packages/coding-agent/src/sdk.ts:495) has customTools and extensions but neither tools nor noTools.
resolution: KEEP omp's interface; retype the harness options to plain `string[]` and map them onto omp's session construction. The 6 DOCUMENTATION_EVAL_TOOLS names ('read','write','edit','grep','find','ls') must be verified to exist in omp's tool registry under those names — if omp renamed any, the control arm silently runs with a smaller toolset, which is exactly the kind of quiet protocol violation these evals exist to prevent.

what: InlineExtension does not exist in omp; omp calls the same concept ExtensionFactory, and the event name used to rewrite the system prompt differs. pi's harness registers a hidden inline extension listening for 'before_agent_start' and replacing the prompt.
resolution: KEEP omp's ExtensionFactory. But do NOT assume the hook name carries over: verify the actual omp hook for pre-prompt system-prompt rewriting. If none exists, add one — this is a legitimate gap, because the entire with_docs/without_docs experiment is defined by a system-prompt difference, and a prompt-rewriting seam is required for ANY doc-lift measurement. Note pi's comment at L388-389: a forced prompt is not recorded in the transcript, which is why the harness keeps the transform's own value.

what: getDocsPath / getExamplesPath / getReadmePath do not exist in omp (0 definitions, verified). test/harness.test.ts imports all three to assert the doc files a variant should or should not have.
resolution: REPLACE, do not re-add. The doc-path helpers pi used are not omp's API. Derive the expected doc paths from omp's own `packages/coding-agent` package.json `files` array, which is the shipped contract — and note it already lists `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` and `examples` but has NO `docs` entry, unlike pi's.

what: The 'docs' directory the whole experiment strips does not exist in the same place. pi deletes packages/coding-agent/{README.md,CHANGELOG.md,docs,examples} in the without_docs image and asserts on exactly that set. omp's coding-agent ships README.md, CHANGELOG.md, examples/ — and no docs/; its user-facing docs live at repo-root ./docs, and its bundle carries an omp-only dist/docs-index.generated.txt that backs the omp:// docs URL scheme.
resolution: RETARGET the doc set, do not delete the concept. The without_docs arm must strip exactly what omp's model can actually see: README.md, CHANGELOG.md, examples/, and dist/docs-index.generated.txt (the omp-only one — stripping it is a NEW arm pi had no equivalent of, and dropping it would leave the treatment reading docs the control cannot). Separately, documentation-audit.eval.ts globs a directory that does not exist in omp and would discover ZERO cases — a silent no-op, the worst failure mode in the package. Either repoint it at omp's real docs or do not port it.

what: pi's release-tarball install pipeline has no omp equivalent. install-runtime.mjs imports getPublicWorkspacePackages/packReleasePackages/installCodingAgentConsumer from scripts/release-packages.mjs and scripts/coding-agent-consumer.mjs — neither file exists in omp. It then installs the packed tarballs and entrypoint.ts asserts pi-coding-agent resolves to dist/index.js with an npm-shrinkwrap.json present.
omp_anchor: mới — không có (omp scripts/ has ci-release-*.ts + release.ts, which publish from source; coding-agent's main is ./src/index.ts and its only dist artifact is dist/cli.js)
resolution: REBUILD, do not port. There is no npm-installable compiled runtime in omp to image. The realistic options are (a) mount the omp workspace source into the container and run the CLI from source with bun — losing the 'resolves from dist' guarantee but gaining fidelity to how developers actually run omp; or (b) extend scripts/release.ts to emit packed tarballs and write the missing consumer helper. Recommend (a) for a first cut: it is smaller, it cannot drift from the source, and the dist-resolution assertion it drops is a pi-release-specific check, not a security control.

what: The 'eval' name collides with a large, unrelated omp subsystem. packages/coding-agent/src/eval/ is 60 files of JS/Python sandbox execution, kernel sessions, speculation evaluators and workpool bridges; packages/coding-agent/src/if-bench/ and src/judgment/ sit next to it. A new packages/evals at repo root does not collide on disk, but 'eval' in an omp code review now means two unrelated things.
resolution: KEEP both, but name the concept in prose. The new package evaluates AGENT BEHAVIOUR (does the agent configure its own installation correctly); the existing eval/ subsystem evaluates UNTRUSTED CODE the agent wrote. Call the new one 'behavioural evals' in docs, changelog and commit messages, and never add it to scripts/ci-test-ts.ts's existing `eval`-named buckets without a comment. Consider a packages/evals/README.md line that says so on the first page.

what: session.resourceLoader does not exist on omp's AgentSession. extensions.docs.eval.ts reads session.resourceLoader.getExtensions() for both the loaded-extension list and the per-extension tool sets. omp exposes session.extensionRunner (a getter at packages/coding-agent/src/session/agent-session.ts:12155) but no resourceLoader.
resolution: REPOINT to omp's extension surface once identified; extensionRunner may be optional (returns `ExtensionRunner | undefined`), so the ported output mapper must handle the undefined case rather than assume it. This eval is the most valuable of the five (it proves an agent can create and then use a tool extension), so it is worth the extra work — but it is a rewrite, not a copy.
